review_contract: Each patch is pinned to an exact trip, input sequence, ordered endpoint path, official train evidence, official physical-line evidence, and one current jp-2025 line identity. Current N02 identity does not establish a daily service-validity interval. The uncalled Nippori boundary is a route-only station identity used solely by trip_line_segments and is not a canonical timetable stop.

new_sources.publisher: 国土交通省 国土数値情報
new_sources.title: 鉄道データ N02 令和7年版
new_sources.notes: Official catalog defines N02_003 as railway line name and N02_004 as operator. The canonical jp-* line ids are deterministic identifiers in the shipped jp-2025 package, not identifiers published by MLIT. This snapshot has no per-line daily validity interval.

new_sources.publisher: 東日本旅客鉄道株式会社
new_sources.title: 旅客営業規則 第156条（途中下車）
new_sources.notes: Article 156 identifies 東海道本線 東京–熱海, 中央本線 東京–塩尻, 東北本線 東京–黒磯, and 常磐線 日暮里–浪江 for its stopover rule, and lists 篠ノ井線 without endpoint bounds. It supports only that named line scope; it does not establish operator ownership, the 篠ノ井–塩尻 endpoints, a train-specific route, or daily-valid current-N02 history.

jr-east-azusa-route-current.locator: The current train-family guide names the Chuo Main Line corridor from Shinjuku through Kofu to Matsumoto; it does not identify the Shiojiri–Matsumoto physical section.

jr-east-chuo-shinonoi-boundary-20260507.locator: Page 1 assigns Chuo Main Line to Takao–Shiojiri and Shinonoi Line to Shiojiri–Shinonoi; it does not identify a jp-* feature id or an Azusa operating day.

jr-east-passenger-lines-rules-20260930.locator: Article 156 names the Tokaido, Chuo, Tohoku and Joban bounds used here and lists Shinonoi Line without endpoints; it does not establish ownership, a train path, a jp-* id, or daily validity.

mlit-n02-2025-20251231.locator: The N02-25 catalog defines the line-name and operator attributes. Canonical jp-* ids and endpoint membership are project-derived from the reviewed shipped snapshot; neither proves a train route or daily line validity.

jr-east-hitachi26-202609.locator: The exact Hitachi 26 table proves the displayed 2026 operating dates and ordered passenger calls from Iwaki through Ueno and Tokyo to Shinagawa, but not the physical line id between calls.

jr-east-tokiwa55-202609-east-next.locator: The exact Tokiwa 55 table proves the displayed 2026 operating dates and ordered passenger calls from Shinagawa through Ueno to Katsuta, but not the physical line id between calls.

jr-east-hitachi-route-current.locator: The current guide says Hitachi and Tokiwa run on the Joban Line and identifies the Shinagawa/Tokyo/Ueno–Mito/Iwaki/Sendai corridor; it is not train-number-specific edge evidence.

jr-east-kanto-route-map-202604.locator: The official network map supports the reviewed Joban station corridor; its drawn line is not treated as a canonical N02 feature id or dated train schedule.

jr-east-ueno-tokyo-line-20150314.locator: The official notice establishes Joban through service via Ueno and Tokyo to Shinagawa. Ueno-Tokyo Line is a service corridor here, not the physical N02 line name.

jr-hokkaido-soya-down-20260930.locator: The selected 2026-09-30 Soya Main Line table proves Sarobetsu 3, its direction and ordered passenger calls; it does not publish the normalized jp-* id.

jr-hokkaido-soya-up-20260930.locator: The selected 2026-09-30 Soya Main Line table proves Sarobetsu 4, its direction and ordered passenger calls; it does not publish the normalized jp-* id.

jr-hokkaido-sarobetsu-family-guide-2026.locator: The current guide identifies Sarobetsu and its Asahikawa–Wakkanai corridor; it does not prove every dated train or a canonical N02 id.

jr-hokkaido-line-inventory-20260401.locator: The 2026-04-01 company inventory identifies Soya Main Line as Asahikawa–Wakkanai under JR Hokkaido; the shipped snapshot uses the normalized name 宗谷線 and a project-derived jp-* id.
